_meta.purpose: Curated reference of published / patent-claimed epitopes on GPC3, for freedom-to-operate (FTO) style epitope screening of new antibody campaigns.
_meta.numbering_convention: All 'uniprot_residues' fields use FULL-LENGTH UniProt P51654 numbering (signal peptide 1-24 included). The companion structure files use MATURE numbering where Q1 == UniProt Q25, i.e. uniprot = mature + 24.

evidence_levels.high: explicit residue numbers or peptide sequence stated in a primary publication or granted patent claim
evidence_levels.medium: residue range stated in review / abstract level source
evidence_levels.low: domain-level assignment only (e.g. 'N-lobe'), no residue numbers

_meta.DISCLAIMER: This is a research triage aid, NOT a legal freedom-to-operate opinion. Epitope overlap is only one factor in antibody patent infringement; most antibody claims are drafted around CDR sequences, not epitopes. A qualified patent attorney must review any commercial program.

epitopes.notes: Immunogen was a C-terminal fragment. Epitope sits close to the GPI anchor / membrane-proximal. Most clinically advanced anti-GPC3 mAb (phase II HCC).
Raised against peptide 511-560. hYP7 is the basis of multiple CAR-T and ADC programs. Very high affinity (Kd ~0.3 nM).

epitopes.owner: academic (Journal of Translational Medicine 2020) + related filings
patents: see J Transl Med 18:295 (2020); associated CN/US filings
epitopes.notes: Alanine-scan hot spots. Epitope lies close to the HS chain modification sites and OUTSIDE the Wnt-binding site. Bridges the C-terminal part of the N-lobe (Y295) with the C-lobe.

epitopes.lobe: N-lobe (requires both N- and C-terminal domains for binding)
epitopes.notes: Binds the membrane-distal tip of the N-lobe. Conformation-specific: binding is lost on denatured GPC3 and requires the intact N+C domain pair. HS-independent. Range given here is the whole N-lobe, so overlap scoring against it is deliberately conservative (worst case).

epitopes.antibody: J80A, F5, C46, I82 (HN3-competing mAb panel)
patents: covered by / related to the HN3 family filings
epitopes.notes: Panel that cross-blocks HN3; mapped with alanine and L428K mutants. Indicates the N-lobe surface is competitively crowded even where exact residues are unpublished.
Binds the heparan sulfate CHAINS, not the protein core. HS attachment serines are S495 and S509. A protein-core binder in this window may still sterically clash with HS chains.
Raised against the C-terminal 70-residue polypeptide. Widely used IHC reagent, contributes to prior-art density in the C-terminal region.

patents: companion filings to the GC33 family
epitopes.notes: Also generated with a C-terminal GPC3 fragment as antigen.

functional_hotspots.notes: Cysteine-rich hydrophobic groove in the N-lobe that binds Wnt. Blocking here is mechanistically attractive (Wnt/beta-catenin blockade) but it is the single most obvious functional site on GPC3, so it is heavily prospected. Treat as high prior-art density even though published residue-level antibody epitopes are sparse.

Furin-like convertase cleaves between Arg358 and Ser359, splitting GPC3 into a ~40 kDa N-subunit and a ~30 kDa C-subunit that remain disulfide-linked. An epitope SPANNING this site is a developability liability: the local conformation differs between uncleaved and cleaved GPC3 on the cell surface.
Heparan sulfate glycosaminoglycan attachment serines. Bulky HS chains here can sterically occlude nearby protein-core epitopes on native cell-surface GPC3.
GPI anchor attachment. Membrane-proximal; epitopes here sit very close to the membrane which can help CAR-T synapse formation but limits IgG access.
